Let <MATH_0001> be a scheme.
<STRUCT_0001>
<STRUCT_0002> We say <MATH_0002> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0001>scheme over <MATH_0003><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> to mean that <MATH_0004>
comes equipped with a morphism of schemes <MATH_0005>.
The morphism <MATH_0006> is sometimes called the
<TEXTITOPEN_0002>structure morphism<TEXTITCLOSE_0002>.
<STRUCT_0003> If <MATH_0007> is a ring we say
<MATH_0008> is a <TEXTITOPEN_0003>scheme over <MATH_0009><TEXTITCLOSE_0003> instead of
<MATH_0010> is a scheme over <MATH_0011>.
<STRUCT_0004> A <TEXTITOPEN_0004>morphism <MATH_0012> of schemes over <MATH_0013><TEXTITCLOSE_0004>
is a morphism of schemes such that the composition
<MATH_0014> of <MATH_0015> with the structure morphism of <MATH_0016> is
equal to the structure morphism of <MATH_0017>.
<STRUCT_0005> We denote <MATH_0018> the set of all morphisms
from <MATH_0019> to <MATH_0020> over <MATH_0021>.
<STRUCT_0006> Let <MATH_0022> be a scheme over <MATH_0023>. Let <MATH_0024> be a
morphism of schemes. The <TEXTITOPEN_0005>base change<TEXTITCLOSE_0005> of <MATH_0025>
is the scheme <MATH_0026> over <MATH_0027>.
<STRUCT_0007> Let <MATH_0028> be a morphism of schemes over <MATH_0029>. Let <MATH_0030>
be a morphism of schemes. The <TEXTITOPEN_0006>base change<TEXTITCLOSE_0006> of <MATH_0031> is
the induced morphism <MATH_0032> (namely the
morphism <MATH_0033>).
<STRUCT_0008> Let <MATH_0034> be a ring. Let <MATH_0035> be a scheme over <MATH_0036>.
Let <MATH_0037> be a ring map. The <TEXTITOPEN_0007>base change<TEXTITCLOSE_0007> <MATH_0038>
is the scheme <MATH_0039>
over <MATH_0040>.
